semantic_findings.title: Unsupported Floating Desk Load-Bearing Assurance
semantic_findings.description: The reference states that domestic desktop boards up to 2.4 meters need no extra support when supported at both ends. It omits material grade, thickness, design load, and connection capacity, so following this assurance could cause sagging or collapse.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 4 explicitly gives a general span assurance without the specifications needed to establish load capacity. Later reinforcement advice does not qualify that assurance.

content.value_statement: Desk and bookcase choices can create cramped seating, wasted storage, and difficult cleaning. This skill uses Chinese renovation references to compare layouts and prepare practical questions.
actual_capabilities: Compare straight, corner, wardrobe-integrated, and double-desk layouts using the included references.
Explain how desktop height, drawer depth, and chair position affect usable leg clearance.
Summarize floating desk support approaches and reference examples of installation failures.
Compare full-wall, low, open, and enclosed bookcases for storage and visual balance.
Suggest glass doors, sliding doors, and mixed storage arrangements for dust control.
Organize answers into conclusions, analysis, practical actions, and common mistakes.
limitations: The Chinese references include extraction noise and captions whose original images are not bundled.
Structural recommendations are not engineering calculations; some span assurances lack specifications and require independent verification.
The skill does not verify material emissions, installation quality, or compliance with local building requirements.
The bundled material does not provide live prices, supplier availability, or construction drawings.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Bookcase Type
prompt_templates.prompt: I have [book quantity] books in [room type]. Compare low and full-wall bookcases using the references. Consider access, cleaning, and visual balance.

prompt_templates.title: Check Drawer Clearance
prompt_templates.prompt: My desk height is [height], drawer depth is [depth], and chair height is [height]. Identify missing measurements and leg-clearance concerns. Suggest questions before ordering.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Integrated Layouts
prompt_templates.prompt: My room measures [dimensions] and includes [doors, windows, bed, wardrobe]. Compare straight and corner desk-bookcase layouts. Flag door conflicts, chair access, and missing information.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Floating Desk Proposal
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this floating desk proposal: [span, material, thickness, supports, wall type, expected load]. Use the references to identify omissions. Separate layout advice from engineering verification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess proposal completeness before professional review

output_examples.input: My 75 cm desk proposal has a full-width drawer. What should I check?
output: Direct answer: Check the clear height below the drawer before approving it.
Analysis: Desktop height alone does not show whether your thighs will fit beneath the drawer.
Practical actions: Measure drawer underside height and test the intended chair position before ordering.
Common mistake: Raising the desktop can improve clearance while creating an uncomfortable arm position.

output_examples.input: I need book storage but do not want the living room to feel crowded.
output: Direct answer: Compare a low bookcase with a mixed open-and-enclosed arrangement.
Analysis: Low cabinets preserve open wall space, while taller cabinets provide more storage.
Practical actions: Count your books, measure the largest volumes, and reserve accessible shelves for frequently used titles.
Common mistake: Adding deep cabinets everywhere can reduce circulation and increase visual clutter.

output_examples.input: Can a two-meter desktop safely span between two cabinets without another support?
output: Direct answer: Span alone cannot establish safety.
Analysis: Material, thickness, expected load, connections, and long-term deflection need assessment.
Practical actions: Obtain a support specification from a qualified installer or engineer before approving the design.
Common mistake: Treating a reference photograph or a general span claim as proof of load capacity.

best_practices: Provide room measurements, furniture positions, user heights, and intended storage needs before requesting a layout comparison.
Test the proposed chair and drawer clearance before committing to custom dimensions.
Have a qualified professional verify wall conditions, connections, loading, and supports before installing floating furniture.
anti_patterns: Copying a furniture photograph without checking dimensions, support details, or everyday use.
Adding full-width drawers before testing usable leg clearance.
Treating general renovation advice as structural certification or evidence of material safety.

faq.question: What does this skill help me plan?
faq.answer: It helps compare desks, bookcases, wardrobe combinations, shared workspaces, and dust-control options using included Chinese renovation references.

faq.question: Does it include software or installation scripts?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed package contains one instruction document and 42 Markdown reference files.

faq.question: Can it certify a floating desk installation?
faq.answer: No. Support safety requires site-specific material, load, wall, and connection checks by a qualified professional.

faq.question: Are the original design photographs included?
faq.answer: No. Many references describe photographs, but the reviewed package contains only Markdown documents.

faq.question: Does it provide current prices or verified suppliers?
faq.answer: No. Source articles contain occasional product mentions and promotional captions, but these are not verified quotations or supplier recommendations.

faq.question: What should I provide for useful advice?
faq.answer: Provide room dimensions, openings, furniture positions, user heights, chair measurements, book sizes, and the proposed desk or cabinet specifications.
